title: Can an improviser have too much technique?
summary: Carter says one cannot have too much technique but can overuse it, citing Trumbauer's restraint.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know, this is a point I was going to raise, too, and you've raised it for me. And let me put the question perhaps in an argumentative way; that is, do you think an improvisor can have too much technique? Is there such a thing?
I don't think he can have too much; I think he can overemploy it, if that says anything.
I think so. Because I think of someone -- well, someone you've said you admired very much, who was Frankie Trumbauer, who indeed, did have great technique.
You better believe it. If you don't
believe it, listen to things like "Trombology" and ...
I'll try to steer clear of naming names here; perhaps you'd just as soon steer clear of that, too.
Well, if it helps us make a point, I will.
Okay. Well, we might indulge that.
